planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, fertile potting mix; Compacta is frost-tender and grown outdoors only in zones 10-11, elsewhere as an indoor foliage plant.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, fertile potting mix. Compacta is a naturally dwarf dieffenbachia, staying noticeably shorter and bushier than standard dumb cane cultivars while carrying the same large, glossy, cream-and-green speckled leaves, making it a better fit for smaller rooms, desks, and tabletops where a full-sized dieffenbachia would grow too tall too quickly. Its more compact internodes give the plant a fuller, denser look sooner without needing to be cut back for shape. Water when the top inch of potting mix dries, avoid cold drafts and temperatures below 60°F, and wear gloves when handling or pruning, since the sap is irritating to skin and toxic if chewed by pets or children.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, fertile potting mix. Reflector carries unusually dark green leaves densely speckled with fine cream to pale yellow spots that seem to shimmer or glow in indirect light, giving it a moodier, more textured look than the lighter, more heavily variegated cultivars like Camille. Its bold, dramatic leaf coloring stands out against paler tropical foliage companions and provides year-round structural interest as an upright floor or tabletop plant depending on pot size. Water when the top inch of potting mix dries, avoid cold drafts and temperatures below 60°F, and wear gloves when handling or pruning, since the sap is irritating to skin and toxic if chewed by pets or children.

common_name: Domino Peace Lily (White-Speckled Variegated Peace Lily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in deep to moderate shade; Domino's variegation is more pronounced with brighter indirect light than plain green peace lily cultivars need.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in deep to moderate shade, keeping the plant warm above 60°F and away from direct sun and drying drafts. Domino is a variegated peace lily cultivar with glossy dark green leaves finely speckled and streaked in white, giving the foliage a mottled, dotted pattern distinct from the plain solid-green leaves of most peace lily cultivars, in addition to the classic white spathe flowers rising above the foliage. It needs slightly brighter indirect light than plain green peace lilies to maintain strong variegation, though still no direct sun. Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged, and expect the leaves to droop dramatically when thirsty, an easy visual cue for watering, recovering within hours once watered.

common_name: Picasso Peace Lily (Bold White-Splashed Peace Lily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in deep to moderate shade; Picasso's variegation is more pronounced with brighter indirect light than plain green peace lily cultivars need.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in deep to moderate shade, keeping the plant warm above 60°F and away from direct sun and drying drafts. Picasso is a novelty variegated peace lily cultivar with bold, irregular, hand-painted-looking splashes of white across each glossy green leaf, a much more dramatic and unpredictable variegation pattern than the fine speckling of Domino, so no two leaves look quite alike. The white spathe flowers are the same as other peace lily cultivars, but the striking foliage is the main draw here. It needs slightly brighter indirect light than plain green peace lilies to maintain strong variegation, though still no direct sun. Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged, and expect leaves to droop when thirsty, recovering within hours once watered.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown clumps in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, fertile soil in shade to part shade; all parts are toxic if ingested.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, fertile soil in shade to part shade. Flame is a clivia selection bred for an especially deep, saturated red-orange flower color, more intensely colored than the softer orange of the wild species, held in the same dramatic umbels of a dozen or more lily-like blooms above broad, strappy, dark evergreen leaves each spring. Like other clivia it thrives in dense shade under trees where few other ornamentals flower well, tolerating drought and being somewhat pot-bound better than most shade perennials, and it actually blooms more reliably when slightly crowded in its container. Divide only when clumps become very congested, since clivia resents frequent disturbance; all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.
